pairs.why: A has the long, translucent arms and the cyan glow along the bell's edge that match the real jellyfish, while B's bunched, frilly arms read as a different build.
B keeps the real key layout with an '=' key and has the same body proportions; A swaps in an oversized '0' key, though both wrongly use white keys instead of navy ones.
B's darker, softer green background and calmer lighting are closer to the real card; A is more crowded and more saturated, though its thicker main branch is a point in its favor.
A fills the frame and has the bold, saturated, glossy plastic of the real duck, while B is small and lit more flatly; both draw the handle wrong.
The two are nearly identical, but B's drop shadow and depth are slightly closer to the real clock's raised look.
A shows the table large and close with chunky stone forms, as the real card does, while B pushes a smaller table into a wide landscape.
A hangs flat on a striped wall like the real clock; B stands on a floor with a ground shadow, which changes the setting.
B's muted darker-green backdrop and softer finish are closer to the real card than A's acid-lime background and denser, harsher stippling.
